subject: botany
question_text: What is the significance of the vacuole in a plant cell?

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack botany section, Chapter 9 'The Unit of Life' (book pp.23-26), which prints the question and a model answer but NO star rank and NO year citations - so stars are 0 and appearances are empty by fact, not by omission. Only ONE source book is held for botany: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no botany board paper is in the corpus. The two-book union check and the back-test are therefore STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE for this card, not merely unrun - never read this as 'checked and clean'. page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Size and tonoplast
lines: In a mature plant cell the vacuole can fill
up to 90 per cent of the cell volume.
It is bound by a single membrane called the
tonoplast and is filled with cell sap.
steps.why: The vacuole is marked as a store, so the answer must first say what holds the store — one membrane, the tonoplast — and how large that store is. The book states the 90 per cent flatly; it is an upper figure for a mature cell, not every cell.
common_mistakes: Writing that the vacuole has a double membrane. The tonoplast is a single membrane.
Saying the vacuole is empty. It is filled with cell sap.
steps.memory_tip: Tonoplast wraps the vacuole, plasma membrane wraps the cell. One membrane each.
steps.margin_note: Two lines: the size and the tonoplast. That is this mark.

steps.label: Functions
lines: It stores water, mineral ions, sugars, waste
anthocyanin, so it is called the store house
The tonoplast moves ions into the sap, water
follows by osmosis, and the cell stays firm.
steps.why: Every function follows from one fact: the tonoplast moves ions into the sap. That makes the sap concentrated, water enters by osmosis, and the pressure inside keeps the cell firm.
common_mistakes: Listing only storage. The turgor and osmoregulation marks are then lost.
Writing that the vacuole makes food. It stores; it does not make.
steps.memory_tip: Three S words: Store, Sap pressure, Salt balance.
steps.margin_note: The boxed line plus two named stored substances completes it.

insider_note: The word in the question is significance, so a list of stored substances alone is half an answer — the turgor point is what completes it.
